data.body:
SESSION (interim, written mid-flight so the findings survive a context loss). Epic 061c: 36 of 38 descendants closed; only eb6e (claimed, in_progress, mine) and 8625 (genuinely blocked — eb6e 'blocks' it and it is absent from 'ready') remain.

CORRECTION TO THE HANDOFF I INHERITED. 2ca9 and 34cd were NOT open with 'closes running'. They were ALREADY CLOSED, verifier-PASS, all ACs ticked. My first reads showed in_progress because the local .tickets-tracker was STALE against origin/tickets, not because a flock write failed. Lesson: a stale read looks exactly like a failed write, and the previous session's 'verify by content' concluded the wrong one.

THE BIGGEST FINDING: eb6e'S CERTIFIED PLAN CONTAINED A FALSE SHOWSTOPPER, and it had already forced a BLOCK and two plan amendments. The claim was that Dockerfile.reviewbot omits --extra bedrock, therefore pydantic_ai.providers.bedrock is absent, therefore the first Bedrock call raises LLMConfigError and the LLM-Review gate stops voting on every landing. MEASURED in the running production container (image built from current main): 'from pydantic_ai.providers.bedrock import BedrockProvider' succeeds, exit 0. The bedrock extra contributes ONLY boto3, which the reviewbot extra already installs at the same version; the provider module ships in the base pydantic-ai-slim wheel and the extra gates its DEPENDENCY, not the module. The reasoning error: absence of the EXTRA was taken to imply absence of the MODULE, and confirmed by READING the Dockerfile rather than EXECUTING the import — including by me ('verified against the tree'). The --extra bedrock edit still lands, reframed as explicitness (the dependency is satisfied only incidentally today). This is the epic's own lesson again: the check shared the claim's assumption.

PRE-CUTOVER VERIFICATION, all inside the production container, none of it touching the service definition: with the three class slots supplied at exec level rebar resolves frontier/standard/trivial to the three bedrock: profiles; with them absent it resolves to anthropic:claude-* (so the Anthropic baseline is EVIDENCED, and the kill switch's subtractive mechanism is DEMONSTRATED); and a real Bedrock call through rebar's own build_bedrock_provider returned CUTOVER_PROBE_OK at 21 in / 11 out. Also: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is present, len 108 (an earlier 'UNSET' read of mine was a shell-quoting artifact that measured the HOST env — discarded). And the PROVENANCE ORACLE IS LIVE: a post-e951 code_review artifact carries provider_provenance provider='anthropic' model='anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6' tier='first_class', so the post-cutover expectation is unambiguous and a null would mean the cutover rather than a broken oracle.

TERRAFORM. main was ALREADY RED on Terraform Drift at e9d4d390c3 — 34cd landed an alarm that was never applied. Plan was '1 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy', so I applied it; drift is now clean and rebar-autodeploy-review-interrupts is live and OK. That also validated apply credentials, which eb6e's alarm criteria depend on. There is NO automated apply: terraform-drift.yml is read-only (ReadOnlyAccess OIDC role), autodeploy does not run terraform, applies are manual.

FOUR DEFECTS FILED, each measured, all linked discovered_from eb6e:
* 61d8-ff23-8ee0-4289 — Bedrock ignores llm_retry_max_attempts and timeout_s; no botocore retry envelope (grep for botocore.config/aws_read_timeout/'adaptive' across src+tests returns NOTHING; the tenacity envelope is anthropic-only).
* 4e71-f237-28c4-4c65 — bedrock_model.py's typed no-region error tells operators to set AWS_REGION, which does not resolve. MEASURED on botocore 1.43.62 with AWS_DEFAULT_REGION genuinely unset via 'env -u': AWS_REGION alone yields region_name None. Pushed as Gerrit 1325 and deliberately HELD OPEN as the cutover drill fixture.
* 1c39-96d4-8f9e-4d38 — Terraform drift never gates a Gerrit change (triggers are pull_request / push-to-main / schedule / dispatch, and a Gerrit change is none of those), so un-applied infra passes Verified and reds main AFTER submit. 34cd is the worked example.
* 9baf-06ce-60ba-4f0b — rebar-gerrit-voter-errors, the alarm eb6e treats as its safety net, has EMPTY AlarmActions and OKActions in HCL and live: it notifies nobody. Audited all 12 live rebar alarms — exactly 2 are silent (voter_errors and replication_errors, both the story-S-numbered files).

WORK AUTHORED. Two stacked Gerrit changes so eb6e's ordering criterion is structural: c8d1685bb1 'Bedrock safety net and packaging' (Dockerfile --extra bedrock, runbook kill-switch entry citing 61d8, and a metric-math Bedrock client-error alarm over AWS/Bedrock native metrics summed across all three ModelIds with a FILL+IF divide-by-zero guard, SNS-wired after I found it silent), then 047764d528 'point the review bot at Bedrock' (the three class slots + REBAR_USAGE_LOG + a 4-assertion pinning test).

A BLOCKER I FOUND AND FIXED: REBAR_USAGE_LOG was set NOWHERE under infra/, and usage recording is opt-in, so the production bot wrote no usage log at all — making the per-call tally criterion unsatisfiable. That tally is the plan's own preferred oracle and the only thing separating 'every call went to Bedrock' from 'most did', since ANTHROPIC_API_KEY deliberately stays in the container. Wired to the persistent volume with the growth quantified (~100-200 MB/year against 44G free), not hand-waved.

TWO PROCESS MISTAKES OF MINE, recorded because the pattern is the point. (1) I mutated a file then restored with 'git checkout --' while my edit was UNCOMMITTED — twice — which silently reverted my own work and confounded three mutation results each time. The tell was the RESTORED baseline not returning to green. Both rounds were re-run against a committed tree with a dirty-tree guard. A mutation experiment is only valid if the restore returns to the state you believe it does. (2) I twice read an exit code through a pipe ('| head', PIPESTATUS in the wrong shell), getting head's status instead of the gate's — the exact trap the handoff warns about.

A HANDOFF ERROR TO CARRY FORWARD: the handoff states 'make lint also runs a COMMENT-HYGIENE check'. IT DOES NOT in this tree — grep of the Makefile finds nothing and it is a separate CI step at .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:130 (scripts/check_comment_hygiene.py). I ran it explicitly on the stacked tree: exit 0. Also: 'rebar list' accepts NEITHER --limit NOR -o json, and passing them yields EMPTY OUTPUT rather than an error, which reads as 'nothing exists'. And bugs/session_logs are EXEMPT from the plan-review claim gate per rebar.toml, so filed bugs can be claimed without paying for a review.
